title: Support awaited cleanup before agent-created worktrees are removed
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

Agent-created worktrees support setup tasks through:

```json
"runOptions": {
  "runOn": "worktreeCreated"
}
```

This makes it possible to provision resources for an isolated agent session, such as:

- A cloned development database
- A worktree-specific environment file and secrets
- A container, service, or allocated port
- Other temporary external resources

However, there is no corresponding supported lifecycle for cleaning up those resources when VS Code removes the worktree.

## Current behavior

1. Configure a `worktreeCreated` task that provisions an external resource.
2. Start an agent session using worktree isolation.
3. Mark the session as Done/archive it.
4. VS Code removes the worktree internally.
5. No workspace task, agent hook, or extension API is invoked and awaited before that removal.

`Stop` hooks are not suitable because they run when an individual agent execution stops. `SessionEnd` is also not equivalent because Mark as Done is an archive operation and does not dispose the session.

Filesystem watchers can detect removal after the fact, but they are not awaited, can miss events while the extension host is unavailable, and cannot reliably access worktree-local cleanup metadata after the directory has gone.

## Requested behavior

Please expose an awaited lifecycle before VS Code removes an agent-created worktree.

A task-based form symmetrical with `worktreeCreated` could look like:

```json
{
  "label": "Clean up agent worktree",
  "type": "shell",
  "command": "pnpm",
  "args": ["cleanup:agent-worktree"],
  "runOptions": {
    "runOn": "worktreeRemoving"
  }
}
```

The cleanup task should:

- Run while the worktree still exists, with the worktree as its working directory.
- Be awaited before worktree removal continues.
- Run for both Mark as Done/archive and permanent session deletion.
- Receive the removal reason and stable session/worktree identity when practical.
- Surface failures instead of silently removing the worktree before cleanup completes. A bounded timeout and an explicit "remove anyway" path would avoid indefinite blocking.

An awaited extension API such as `workspace.onWillRemoveAgentWorktree`, with an event `waitUntil(...)` mechanism, would provide the same underlying capability.

This would let workspace tooling manage the lifecycle of resources provisioned for isolated agent sessions. A separate reconciliation mechanism would still be needed for crashes or forced termination, but normal VS Code-initiated cleanup could be deterministic.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.132.0
- Commit: df53daabb18cd157bdb08c7f01c34df936cf12f4c
- OS: Windows x64

title: Fix compact menu issues and add regression tests
body:
This pull request addresses several issues related to the compact menu in Visual Studio Code, specifically focusing on the stale state of overflow actions and menu dismissal behavior. The changes include:

- **Bug Fixes**:
  - Implemented lazy composition for overflow actions when the Application Menu or More menu is opened, resolving stale state issues in both compact and non-compact modes.
  - Ensured that compact composition starts at menu index 0, independent of any deferred layout state.

- **Testing Enhancements**:
  - Added regression tests to cover the new behavior, ensuring that the fixes are validated across both Electron and Chromium environments.
  - Removed unnecessary assertions and focused tests on relevant behaviors, improving test reliability.

These changes were made in response to user feedback and are intended to enhance the overall user experience by ensuring that the compact menu behaves consistently and as expected.

No line = not migrated. - *Disk:* migrated when `/agentSessionData//session.db` (with a working directory) exists. - *UI:* migrated row is deduped to `agent-host-copilotcli:` and becomes editable. - *Telemetry*: Do `Show Telemetry` and look for event `agentHost.legacyCopilotCliMigration` - Run each numbered case in **both** the Chat Editor and the Agents Window unless stated otherwise. ## Prep This testing requires you have few extension host based Copilot CLI sessions already created and available. Creation of legacy CLI session will be disabled soon, hence users won't hit it. --- ## A. Setting gating ### A1. Feature OFF by default - [ ] Fresh profile, do **not** set `chat.agentSessions.migrateLegacyCopilotCli`. - [ ] Have at least one pre-existing legacy Copilot CLI session on disk. - [ ] Open the session list. - **Expected:** Legacy session opens with the old behavior (no migration); it is **not** surfaced as migratable; no agent-host metadata is written. --- ## B. Migrate on OPEN (core behavior) ### B1. Migration happens only on explicit open - [ ] Setting ON. Have several un-migrated legacy sessions. - [ ] Open the session list, let it render, and scroll through it. **Do not click any session.** - **Expected:** No session is migrated by being displayed (no `[Copilot] Adopting…` log; no `agentSessionData//` folder created). ### B2. Hover does NOT migrate - [ ] Setting ON. Hover over a migratable legacy row (tooltip/preview) without opening it. - **Expected:** No migration — no log line, no `agentSessionData//` folder; row stays migratable. ### B3. Opening a legacy session migrates it - [ ] Setting ON. Click/open one un-migrated legacy session. - **Expected:** Session opens, full history loads, and it migrates in place (one `[Copilot] Adopting…` log; `agentSessionData//` created). Row now behaves as a native agent-host session. ### B4. Migrated session is editable / continuable - [ ] After B3, send a new message in the migrated session. - **Expected:** The turn runs normally against the agent host; history + new turn persist. ### B5. Re-opening an already-migrated session - [ ] Open a session that was already migrated earlier. - **Expected:** Opens directly as an agent-host session; no re-migration (no new log line); history intact. ### B6. Deduplication of the legacy row - [ ] Setting ON. Migrate a session, observe the list. - **Expected:** Only **one** entry is shown (the `agent-host-copilotcli:` row); the stale `copilotcli:` legacy duplicate is gone. --- ## D. Startup ### D1. Agents Window standalone - [ ] Launch the Agents Window without the main workbench chat editor in use. Setting ON. - **Expected:** Legacy sessions surface and migrate-on-open works (migrate flag forwarded from the Agents window itself). ### D2. Chat Editor only - [ ] Use only the Chat Editor with the setting ON (Agents Window closed). - **Expected:** Same surfacing + migrate-on-open behavior. ### D3. Both windows open simultaneously - [ ] Open both surfaces with the setting ON. - **Expected:** Both show the same migratable set; migrating in one reflects in the other; no flip-flop of the migrate flag. --- ## E. Cross-surface consistency ### E1. Migrate in Agents Window, view in Chat Editor - [ ] With both open, migrate a legacy session from the Agents Window. - **Expected:** Chat Editor reflects it as migrated (dedup applied, no stale legacy row). ### E2. Migrate in Chat Editor, view in Agents Window - [ ] Reverse of E1. - **Expected:** Agents Window reflects the migration; single migrated row. ### E3. Open the same legacy session from both surfaces - [ ] Open the same un-migrated session from one surface, then the other. - **Expected:** Single migration (idempotent — only one log line total); no duplicate metadata; identical history. --- ## F. Content integrity after migration ### F1. History fidelity - [ ] Migrate a legacy session with a rich history (multiple turns, tool calls, edits). - **Expected:** All turns, tool invocations, and file-change summaries render correctly; ordering preserved. ### F2. Working directory / project association - [ ] Migrate a session created against a specific folder/workspace. - **Expected:** Migrated session shows the correct working directory / project. ### F3. Custom title carried over - [ ] Migrate a legacy session that had a user-chosen title. - **Expected:** Migrated session keeps the same title (not regenerated). ### F4. Checkpoints / restore points - [ ] Migrate a session that had legacy checkpoints. - **Expected:** Checkpoints are migrated and usable. --- ## G. Edge cases & resilience ### G1. Archived / read state preserved - [ ] Migrate a legacy session that was archived or marked read. - **Expected:** Archived/read status carried over. ### G2. Toggle setting while a session is open - [ ] Migrate a session, turn the setting OFF, reload. - **Expected:** Already-migrated session still opens as agent-host; new un-migrated sessions are no longer surfaced. --- ## H. Regressions ### H1. Native agent-host copilot sessions unaffected - [ ] With setting ON, confirm existing native agent-host copilot sessions open, run, and list normally. - **Expected:** No change; they are never tagged migratable. ### H2. Non-Copilot providers unaffected - [ ] Confirm Claude/Codex/other provider sessions are untouched by the migration path. - **Expected:** No surfacing/migration applied to non-Copilot-CLI sessions. ### H3. Live status of list not degraded - [ ] With setting ON, verify running/idle status of normal sessions still updates. - **Expected:** Passive list status still works for non-migratable sessions.

title: agentHost: describe entry persistence with a static config table
body:
Fixes the tunnel connection failure reported as:

> Failed to connect to tunnel 'CPC-aamun-ILU2J': Unable to write file `vscode-userdata:/c:/Users/…/settings.json` (NoPermissions (FileSystemError): EPERM: operation not permitted, rename `settings.json.vsctmp` -> `settings.json`)

Supersedes #329634, which fixed the same symptom with an exhaustive switch. This takes the structural route instead, and also fixes a second bug found along the way.

## The problem

Entries were persisted by branching on `RemoteAgentHostEntryType` in about a dozen places, and "this type is not persisted" was expressed by `entryToRawEntry` returning `undefined` and getting dropped by `.filter(isDefined)`.

So registering a tunnel still called `updateValue('chat.remoteAgentHosts', …)` — writing an array **byte-identical** to what was already on disk. On Windows that write can fail with `EPERM` when the atomic `.vsctmp` rename hits a file lock (AV, indexer, another editor). Because the write was `await`ed inline in the connect path, the rejection propagated into `tunnelAgentHostServiceImpl`, which caught it, called `disconnect(connectionId)`, and **tore down a perfectly healthy tunnel**.

## The change

Collect the per-type differences into a static `IRemoteAgentHostEntryTypeConfig` table, modelled on `IPluginFormatConfig`. Each connection type declares its durable `store`, whether it is self-connecting, whether its address is normalized, and how it converts to/from its persisted form.

| Type | `store` | self-connecting |
|---|---|---|
| WebSocket | `settings` | yes |
| SSH | `storage` | no |
| WSL / Tunnel / CloudSandbox | `runtime` | no |

The table is an exhaustive mapped type, so **adding a connection type is now a compile error** rather than an entry that silently vanishes on save.

This absorbs and deletes `entryToRawEntry`, `rawEntryToEntry` (including its flat-shape SSH sniffing, `if (raw.sshConfigHost || raw.sshHostName || …)`) and the `getEntryAddress` switch, and collapses the duplicated upsert/merge helpers and the four configuration-scope helpers into one each.

## Two fixes follow from the model

1. **The reported bug.** Entries whose store is `runtime` are never written, so connecting *or disconnecting* a tunnel, WSL or cloud sandbox host now performs no I/O at all. Settings and storage writes are additionally skipped when the value is unchanged.

2. **A second, unreported bug.** `_reconcileConnections` built `desired` only from persisted entries, then disconnected every `_entries` key not in it — so runtime connections were always eligible for teardown. The label-formatter loop 7 lines above already guarded with `_registeredEntries`; the connection-removal loop had simply missed it. Net effect today: **an unrelated SSH connect silently kills a live tunnel**, since the SSH storage write fires reconcile. There was no test covering this.

## Behaviour

No user-visible behaviour change beyond the two bugs above. Storage locations, storage targets, the settings schema and the `IRemoteAgentHostService` interface are all unchanged; the legacy SSH-in-settings migration still runs.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` clean (two `assignmentService.ts` errors are pre-existing on `main`, verified by typechecking `origin/main` directly)
- `layersChecker` clean
- ESLint clean on all changed files
- 86 tests passing across `remoteAgentHostService` + `sshRemoteAgentHostService`

New coverage: managed connect/remove of Tunnel/WSL/CloudSandbox performs **zero** `updateValue` and zero storage writes; a live tunnel survives both a settings change and a reconcile; config round-trips for WebSocket and SSH; legacy migration still works.

Manual verification of the original repro (exclusive lock on `settings.json` while connecting a tunnel) is worth a pass before merge, since no unit test can reproduce a real Windows file lock.

title: Agent's built-in browser screenshot tool fails with 400 upstream error on BYOK vision model (MiMo, via OpenCode Zen), while manually pasted screenshots work fine
body:
Environment
VS Code Copilot Chat (Agent/Autopilot mode)
Model: MiMo (BYOK via OpenCode Zen API endpoint)
OS: Windows
Description

When the Copilot Chat agent uses its built-in browser tool to take a screenshot (e.g. to verify a UI change), the vision request to the BYOK provider fails with a 400 error. When I manually take a screenshot and paste/attach it into the chat myself, the same model reads it without any problem.

The agent/Autopilot's own automatic retries always fail too — every automatic retry attempt gets the same 400 error. The request only succeeds after I manually click the "Try Again" button myself.

By contrast, two other ways of getting a screenshot to the model both work reliably, every time:

Manually taking a screenshot myself and pasting/attaching it into the chat.
Using VS Code's built-in browser "Add Screenshot to Chat" feature.

Only the agent's own automated in-session screenshot action (taken autonomously during an Autopilot run to verify a change) fails, and it only succeeds once I intervene and click "Try Again" myself.

Steps to Reproduce
Configure Copilot Chat with a BYOK vision-capable model (MiMo via OpenCode Zen endpoint).
Start an Agent/Autopilot session that makes a UI change and then has the agent autonomously take a screenshot (via the built-in browser tool) to verify the change.
Observe the screenshot request fails with a 400 error.
Note that the tool's own automatic retries also fail — the request only succeeds after I manually click "Try Again".
Compare with: manually taking a screenshot and pasting it into chat, or using the browser's "Add Screenshot to Chat" button — both succeed on the first try, every time, with the same model.
Expected Behavior

Screenshots captured autonomously by the agent during an Autopilot run should be sent to BYOK vision models in a way the provider accepts, matching the reliability of a manually pasted screenshot or the "Add Screenshot to Chat" button.

Actual Behavior

The agent's autonomous screenshot requests always fail with a 400 error on the first attempt, and the tool's own automatic retries also fail. The request only succeeds once I manually click "Try Again".

Error Details

------
Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.
Client Request Id: 9cc2f078-bfda-424c-8071-079d04ac3a51
Reason: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Error from provider (Console): Upstream request failed: [400] Provider returned error"}}: Error: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Error from provider (Console): Upstream request failed: [400] Provider returned error"}}
    at GG._provideLanguageModelResponse (d:\apps\Microsoft VS Code\<build>\resources\app\extensions\copilot\dist\extension.js:1690:14392)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    at async GG.provideLanguageModelResponse (d:\apps\Microsoft VS Code\<build>\resources\app\extensions\copilot\dist\extension.js:1690:15505)
-------



Follow-up log entries — these appear even though the underlying request is still failing and needs a manual retry:

Autopilot recovered from a request error
Autopilot recovered from a request error
Autopilot recovered from a request error

--------

Suspected Cause (unconfirmed)

The image payload generated when the agent autonomously takes a screenshot (possibly full-viewport/full-page resolution, or a different format/encoding) may differ from the payload produced by a manual paste or the "Add Screenshot to Chat" button — both of which work reliably with the same model. That difference may be exceeding a size or format constraint enforced by the BYOK provider, causing the automated request to be rejected every time until manually retried.

Additional Notes
This does not appear to be a model-side issue, since the same model reliably accepts screenshots from two other paths (manual paste, "Add Screenshot to Chat").
The tool's own automatic retry does not resolve it — only a manual "Try Again" click does, which suggests the automated retry may be resending an equivalent/identical payload rather than something different.
Happy to provide the full extension log or additional repro details if useful.

body:
Suddenly in later VS Code version GitHub Copilot is again accepting the "Up" arrow to _replace the currently edited text with previous submissions" in the chat interface. This is a regression of #276373 .

From #276373 I already have the following in my key bindings:

```json
  {
    "key": "up",
    "command": "-history.showPrevious",
    "when": "historyNavigationBackwardsEnabled && historyNavigationWidgetFocus && !isComposing && !suggestWidgetVisible"
  },
  {
    "key": "down",
    "command": "-history.showNext",
    "when": "historyNavigationForwardsEnabled && historyNavigationWidgetFocus && !isComposing && !suggestWidgetVisible"
  },
```

Now it seems however that the `when` clause in the keybindings has been changed to:

```
historyNavigationBackwardsEnabled && historyNavigationWidgetFocus && !suggestWidgetVisible
```

This was sort of secretly shoved in and gets around my earlier suppression of this behavior.

Going forward, do I need to _keep_ the overrides above, and add another two?

```json
  {
    "key": "up",
    "command": "-history.showPrevious",
    "when": "historyNavigationBackwardsEnabled && historyNavigationWidgetFocus && !suggestWidgetVisible"
  },
  {
    "key": "down",
    "command": "-history.showNext",
    "when": "historyNavigationForwardsEnabled && historyNavigationWidgetFocus && !suggestWidgetVisible"
  }
```

Or will the new `when` now work for both?

Or has the `when` usage been permanently changed, so that only the latter is relevant?

This shows also that key binding overrides are fragile when VS Code decides to change how the key binding `when` clauses are defined with no warning.

title: Settings Sync does not sync profile associations across machines
body:
Type: Feature Request

VS Code version: 1.132.0 (df53daa, arm64)
OS version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84)
Settings Sync: enabled

### Summary

Settings Sync syncs profiles themselves — their settings, extensions, keybindings, snippets — but it does not sync **which profile a given folder/workspace is associated with**. That association lives only in local machine state (`profileAssociations` in `globalStorage/storage.json`), so on every new machine each folder silently reopens in the Default profile until the user manually re-associates it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On machine A, with Settings Sync enabled, create a profile (e.g. `MuleSoft`).
2. Open a project folder and switch it to that profile. Reopen the folder — it correctly comes back in `MuleSoft`.
3. Sign in to Settings Sync on machine B and clone/open the same folder.

**Expected:** the folder opens in `MuleSoft`, as it does on machine A.
**Actual:** the profile `MuleSoft` has synced and is available, but the folder opens in Default. The association has to be recreated by hand on every machine.

### Why this is not #173768

[#173768](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/173768) asked for assigning a profile via workspace settings and was closed as completed, on the grounds that "associating a profile to a workspace is remembered." That is true *per machine*, and it's the right design for the single-machine case.

The multi-machine case was raised in that thread but never tracked:

> "it's really remember the profile with workspace or visited directory, so the one case when the property need is syncing with different device"

The response there was that docs would be updated. Docs don't close this gap — the behavior itself is what's missing, so I'm filing it separately.

### Framing

This reads more like a **Settings Sync coverage gap** than a new feature: profiles already sync, and the association map is the one remaining piece of profile state that doesn't. Syncing it would make an already-supported workflow survive a machine change.

Path-based associations obviously don't transfer cleanly when a repo lives at different absolute paths on different machines, which is presumably part of why this isn't already done. A few options, roughly in order of how invasive they are:

1. **Sync the association map, match on best-effort basis.** Sync `profileAssociations` and fall back to Default when a path doesn't resolve on the local machine. Simple; works for anyone who keeps a consistent directory layout.
2. **Key associations on something portable** — e.g. git remote URL or workspace-file name — instead of, or in addition to, the absolute path.
3. **Let the workspace opt in.** A `profile` hint in `.code-workspace` / `.vscode/settings.json` naming a profile by name, applied only if a profile with that name already exists locally, and ignorable/promptable for trust reasons. This is the part of #173768 that got closed, but it solves the sync case as a side effect and is the only option that also works for a team sharing a repo.

Any of these would resolve it for me — (1) is the smallest change and would cover the reported case.

### Additional context

Real-world setup: a MuleSoft workspace repo that needs a specific extension set (Mule DX extension pack and friends) which I deliberately keep out of my Default profile. The profile is exactly the right tool and works perfectly on one machine; it's only the "set it up again on each machine" step that undermines it.

title: Customizations: consolidate the two independent "disabled" stores
body:
### Problem

Whether a chat customization is "disabled" is tracked in **two independent, unsynchronised stores**:

| # | Store | Storage key | Scope / target | Serialization | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `IPromptsService.get/setDisabledPromptFiles(type)` (`promptsServiceImpl.ts`) | `chat.disabledPromptFiles.<PromptsType>` | `PROFILE` / `USER` | `uri.toJSON()` + `URI.revive()` | the **Disable/Enable** actions in `aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts` |
| 2 | `AgentCustomizationSyncProvider` (`ICustomizationSyncProvider`) | `customizationSync.disabled.<harnessId>` | `PROFILE` / `MACHINE` | `uri.toString()` | only `pluginListWidget.ts` (plugins) |

Nothing keeps them in agreement, and they differ in storage target (`USER` vs `MACHINE`, so one syncs across machines and the other does not) and in URI serialization.

Consumers pick one essentially at random:

- `enumerateLocalCustomizationsForHarness` read store 2 only.
- `PureItemProviderItemSource` read neither.
- `ItemProviderItemSource` reads store 1.
- The older sessions tree view (`aiCustomizationTreeViewViews.ts`) reads store 1.

This is the direct cause of #329751, where the Agents window wrote to store 1 and every relevant consumer read store 2. It produced a particularly confusing symptom: the older sessions tree view *did* reflect the disabled state, so the same skill appeared disabled in one surface and enabled in another, while the agent host kept receiving it either way.

### Why this is worth fixing structurally

The immediate fix for #329751 makes the agent-host wire consult *both* stores (`syncProvider.isDisabled(uri) || userDisabled.has(uri)`). That resolves the user-visible bug but entrenches the split: every future consumer now has to remember to OR the two together, and every future writer has to pick the right one. The bug is likely to recur in the next surface that ships.

### Suggested direction

Consolidate on a single source of truth for "is this customization disabled", most naturally on `IPromptsService`, with the sync provider's per-harness store either folded into it or kept strictly as a harness-scoped overlay with an explicit, documented precedence rule. Whichever way it goes, there should be exactly one function that answers the question, and the storage target and URI serialization should be consistent.

The two stores and the requirement to consult both are documented for now in `src/vs/sessions/AI_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md` under *Built-in Skills → Enabling and Disabling Built-in Skills*.

Found while investigating #329751.

1. Install an extension or plugin that contributes a chat customization (an instruction, skill, prompt, …).
2. Open the **Customizations** editor and select that item.
3. Invoke **Open** from its context menu.

**Expected:** the file opens read-only, with the message *"This file is provided by a plugin or extension and cannot be edited."*

**Actual:** the file opens fully editable. Users can edit files that live inside an extension's install directory, where their changes will be silently discarded on the next extension update.

### Root cause

`extractSource()` in `aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts` reads the wrong property:

```ts
function extractSource(context: AICustomizationContext): AICustomizationSource | undefined {
	if (URI.isUri(context) || typeof context === 'string') {
		return undefined;
	}
	return context.storage;   // <-- the menu context has `source`, not `storage`
}
```

The context object built by `aiCustomizationListWidget.ts` (both the inline action bar and the right-click menu) is:

```ts
const context: Record<string, unknown> = {
	uri: element.uri.toString(),
	name: element.name,
	promptType: element.promptType,
	source: element.source,          // <-- `source`
	pluginUri: element.pluginUri?.toString(),
	itemId: element.id,
};
```

There is no `storage` property, so `extractSource()` always returns `undefined`. It type-checks only because `AICustomizationContext` has an `[key: string]: unknown` index signature and declares `storage?: PromptsStorage` — a field nothing ever populates.

### Impact

`extractSource()` has two call sites:

- **Open** (`aiCustomizationManagement.openFile`) — the read-only guard `source === extension || source === plugin` never fires. This is the user-visible bug above. The **Open** menu item has no `when` clause, so it is offered for every item including extension- and plugin-provided ones.
- **Delete** (`aiCustomizationManagement.delete`) — the in-action `source` guards (the plugin *"uninstall the entire plugin?"* prompt, and the *"Cannot Delete Extension File"* dialog) are dead code. **No data-loss risk**, because the Delete menu item itself is correctly gated by `WHEN_ITEM_IS_DELETABLE`, which uses the `AI_CUSTOMIZATION_ITEM_STORAGE_KEY` context key — and *that* key is correctly populated from `element.source`. The guards are unreachable defence-in-depth rather than the active protection.
- Delete telemetry (`chatCustomizationEditor.deleteItem`) records `storage: source ?? ''`, so that dimension is always the empty string.

### Suggested fix

Read `context.source` instead of `context.storage`, and drop the unused `storage?: PromptsStorage` field from `AICustomizationContext` so the type reflects what the widget actually sends. Note the declared return type is `AICustomizationSource` while the (unused) field is typed `PromptsStorage` — worth reconciling at the same time.

Found while investigating #329751.

title: Built-in skills cannot be disabled from the Customizations UI in the Agents window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (`main`, found via source analysis)
- OS Version: N/A (platform-independent)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the **Agents** window.
2. Open the **Customizations** editor and select the **Skills** section.
3. Find a skill under the **Built-in** group and invoke **Disable** from its context menu.

**Expected:** the skill is shown as disabled and is no longer sent to the agent host.

**Actual:** nothing happens. The skill stays enabled in the list, and it is still bundled and sent to the agent host. The setting *is* persisted to storage — it just is never read back.

### Root cause

There are two independent "disabled" stores for customizations:

| Store | Storage key | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `IPromptsService.get/setDisabledPromptFiles(type)` | `chat.disabledPromptFiles.<type>` | the **Disable/Enable** actions in `aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts` |
| `AgentCustomizationSyncProvider.isDisabled(uri)` | `customizationSync.disabled.<harnessId>` | only `pluginListWidget.ts` (plugins) |

The Disable action writes to store #1, but the two places that matter in the Agents window read only store #2 (or neither):

1. `enumerateLocalCustomizationsForHarness` (`agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts`) computed `disabled` from `syncProvider.isDisabled(uri)` only, so a user-disabled built-in skill still made it into the synced bundle and was shipped to the agent host.
2. `SessionsCustomizationHarnessService` registers no built-in harnesses, so `isAgentHostTarget()` always matches in the Agents window and `aiCustomizationItemsModel` always selects `PureItemProviderItemSource`. That source built its list purely from the provider (i.e. from the bundle) and never consulted `getDisabledPromptFiles`.

Net effect: the Disable button rendered, wrote to storage, and nothing downstream ever read it.

### Notes for the fix

Both ends have to change together. Fixing only the bundling side makes a disabled built-in skill drop out of the bundle, so the provider stops reporting it and it **disappears from the Skills list entirely** — leaving no way to re-enable it, since the **Enable** menu item is gated on `disabled === true`. The item source must therefore also merge built-in skills in directly from the prompts service so they stay listed while disabled.

Related: #329753 (the two-store split that caused this).

title: Stop auto-update policy from being overridden per extension
body:
Fixes #325909.

I went looking into why the auto-update policy wasn't sticking, and it turns out there are three separate ways around it once `extensions.autoUpdate` is locked by an org policy.

The per-extension "Auto Update" checkbox writes an extension id to a storage-backed opt-out list, and `shouldAutoUpdateExtension` honors that list unconditionally — it never checks whether the top-level value came from policy. So a user can uncheck auto-update for a specific extension and it'll actually stop updating, policy or not.

"Disable Auto Update for Extensions" is worse: it doesn't go through configuration at all for the actual enforcement, it pins every installed extension directly via `updateMetadata({ pinned: true })`. Pinned extensions never auto-update, full stop, regardless of anything else. That's exactly what the issue reporter saw — clicking it clears every extension's checkbox.

And the publisher-level toggle lets someone opt a publisher's extensions back in when policy has auto-update forced off.

None of this is really a UI bug so much as the enforcement never being policy-aware in the first place. So an org that turns this policy on specifically to guarantee security patches land could have that quietly undone extension by extension, without anything telling them it happened.

Fix is a small `isAutoUpdateConfigLockedByPolicy()` check (backed by `configurationService.inspect(...).policyValue`) plus a context key for it, wired into three places: `shouldAutoUpdateExtension` now ignores the override lists while locked, `updateAutoUpdateForAllExtensions` becomes a no-op while locked (so the pinning bypass can't fire), and the per-extension checkbox / the three related commands grey out so the UI stops implying you can change something you actually can't.

Ran the full `ExtensionsWorkbenchServiceTest` suite (89 tests) plus two new ones covering the locked-by-policy cases specifically — all passing. Also ran `npm run typecheck-client` clean.

title: Fix extensions.allowed schema flagging valid version arrays as invalid
body:
## Summary
Fixes #327194.

The `extensions.allowed` JSON schema declares two `patternProperties` regexes: one matching `publisher.extension` keys (allows boolean/string/array-of-versions), and one matching publisher-only keys (allows boolean/string only). Both were anchored only at the end (`$`), not the start.

Because neither pattern was anchored at the start, a key like `ms-vscode.cpptools` matched **both** patterns — the publisher-only pattern matched by latching onto the `cpptools` suffix. JSON Schema requires a value to be valid against every pattern it matches, so an array value like `["1.31.4"]` (valid under the extension-id pattern) failed validation against the publisher-only pattern, producing a false "Incorrect type. Expected one of boolean, string." warning in `settings.json`, even though the setting still worked correctly at runtime.

This likely went unnoticed until a recent `vscode-json-languageservice` bump (#325505) started correctly enforcing validation against every matching `patternProperties` pattern.

## Changes
- Anchor both patterns with `^` so they're mutually exclusive.
- The extension-id pattern, once anchored, is identical to the existing `EXTENSION_IDENTIFIER_PATTERN` constant, so it's reused directly instead of duplicating the regex inline.
- Added `EXTENSION_PUBLISHER_IDENTIFIER_PATTERN` as a named constant for the publisher-only pattern, mirroring the existing convention.
- Added a regression test asserting the two patterns are mutually exclusive for a compound key.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck-client` passes
- [x] Added unit test in `extensionManagement.test.ts` verifying `ms-vscode.cpptools` matches only the extension-id pattern and `ms-vscode` matches only the publisher pattern; ran via the Node test runner (`extension identifier pattern and publisher identifier pattern are mutually exclusive (#327194)` passes)
- [x] Manually verified via regex simulation that `["1.31.4"]` would no longer be double-validated against the incompatible publisher-only schema

body: Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318578 - [x] anyOS @sbatten - [x] windows @amunger Complexity: 3 --- ## Context The Agents window used to force GitHub sign-in with a modal you couldn't dismiss. That was always wrong: GitHub is a requirement of a *particular* agent or model, not of the window itself. If Claude can run on your own Anthropic credentials, there's no reason to make you sign in first. So now it doesn't. When you're signed out and at least one session type can run on its own credentials, the window just opens, and a notification explains what happened and offers sign-in for anyone who actually meant to use their Copilot subscription. This is behind an experimental setting that is **off by default**. Rolling it out for real is #329671. ## TL;DR Sign out of GitHub, make sure Claude has your own Anthropic credentials, and use the Agents window. Tell me whether being let in without signing in feels right — and whether it's clear what you can and can't do while signed out. That's the whole ask. If you'll explore that well on your own, you don't need to read the rest closely. ## Prereqs Three things, all required: 1. **Give Claude a native credential.** In `~/.claude/settings.json` (`%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json` on Windows): ```json { "env": { "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "" } } ``` `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` works too (with a token from `claude setup-token` cmd), and either one is also picked up straight from your environment. 2. Start an insiders with `code-insiders --transient` so you're not signed in 3. **Turn the setting on** (in the Agents window's settings): ```json "chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable": true ``` ## The main thing Open the Agents window signed out. You should land straight in it, with Claude selected and a notification saying **"We've discovered your existing Claude configuration."** Poke at it: * Start a session and actually run a turn. Does it work? * Open the model picker. You should only see Anthropic-native models — no Copilot-routed ones, since there's no Copilot to route through. * The notification has three affordances: **Sign in to GitHub**, an **X**, and a bell-slash **Don't Show Again**. Try each. X should be for this window only (it comes back on reload); the bell-slash should stick. * Take the **Sign in to GitHub** path and finish signing in. Does the window settle into a sensible signed-in state? Do Copilot-routed models show up? I'm most interested in the judgment call here: does being let in without signing in feel like a courtesy or like something is half-configured? Is the notification's wording doing enough work? One thing to keep in mind, this is kinda a point in time experience. Eventually the Agents Window will get an OOBE that will allow for a more streamlined onboarding and the ability to quickly add multiple providers. ## Known issues — please don't file duplicates * **#329667** — Copilot Agent Host with BYOK models can't be used signed out yet. * **#329668** — Codex's signed-out behavior is tracked on its own; don't judge it by what Claude does here. > If something looks like a general Agents window problem rather than a signed-out problem, check whether it reproduces while signed in. That'll help narrow down where the bug actually lives.

title: New TAS assignments endpoint updates (lifecycle, readiness, disposal)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #329653 addressing post-merge review feedback. Hardens the lifecycle of the new TAS assignments endpoint integration in both VS Code core and the Copilot extension: reliable client re-creation on late account/token load, correct disposal semantics, and
neutralization of superseded in-flight clients so they cannot clobber shared state.

## Changes

**Core (`WorkbenchAssignmentService`)**
- **Reliable late-endpoint activation:** the initial account load opens the readiness  barrier without firing `onDidChangeDefaultAccount`, so the assignments endpoint could be  missed on a clean startup (staying legacy-only). Now also re-checks the endpoint after  `getDefaultAccount()` resolves (no extra network refresh), in addition to account-change  events.
- **Superseded-client neutralization:** each setup gets its own revocable storage,  telemetry, and assignments-fetch wrappers. When a setup is superseded or the service is  disposed, the previous wrappers become no-ops, so a still-in-flight client can no longer
  write the shared memento, emit telemetry, or hit the assignments endpoint. (`tas-client`'s  `dispose()` only stops the polling timer, not an in-flight fetch.) Shared services are  referenced lazily to respect constructor init order.
- Registered the setup `DisposableStore` so the final providers/subscriptions are disposed  on teardown (re-setup still `clear()`s it).
- Call `dispose()` directly on the tas-client instead of an `unknown` cast.

**Copilot extension (`BaseExperimentationService`)**
- Announce treatment changes after a replacement delegate finishes its initial fetch,  guarded by a delegate generation so superseded fetches are ignored — experiment-backed  config no longer stays stale until the hourly refresh.
- Call `delegate.dispose()` directly (the `vscode-tas-client` type now declares it),  removing the `unknown` cast.
- Added focused tests for delegate recreation: old-delegate disposal, ignoring a superseded  fetch, and signaling changes after the replacement fetch.

**Docs**
- Corrected the release-date encoding comment (the `yyyymmddHH` value does not fit within  int32) in both the core and Copilot copies.

title: agentHost:  EH Copilot CLI migration updates (prompt scaffolding, worktree, Agents Window reset) + telemetry
body:
Fixes few issues in the adopt-on-open migration of legacy extension-host (EH) Copilot CLI sessions into the agent host, and adds telemetry to measure the migration.

### 1. Strip prompt scaffolding from migrated user messages
EH Copilot CLI persists the *display-wrapped* prompt in `user.message.content` — the raw text followed by `<reminder>` / `<attachments>` / `<userRequest>` scaffolding. The live EH UI strips this, but the agent-host restore path (`mapSessionEvents`) rendered `content` verbatim, so a migrated session showed the whole blob (or, for wrapper-only content, a **blank** message).

`stripPromptScaffolding` now recovers the user's actual text: it removes the auxiliary blocks and keeps the leading raw prompt (mirroring the extension-side `stripReminders`), and falls back to the `<userRequest>` inner text when removal would leave nothing — so `hi`, `hi …<userRequest>hi</userRequest>`, `/remote …<userRequest></userRequest>`, and wrapper-only `<userRequest>hi</userRequest>` all map correctly.

### 2. Bridge worktree metadata on adoption
When a legacy session ran inside a git **worktree**, adoption seeded `isolation: folder` and no worktree metadata, so the migrated session lost repository grouping and its diff base branch. New `WorktreeIsolation.adoptExistingWorktreeMetadata` detects a linked worktree and persists `branchName` / `path` / `repositoryRoot` (+ diff base) — parity with native worktree-isolated sessions — without registering the worktree as host-created (so disposing the session never deletes the user's worktree).

### 3. Fix Agents Window reset-to-default after opening a legacy session
Opening a surfaced adoptable session in the Agents Window briefly showed it, then reset to the "New session" composer; reopening worked. Root cause: after adoption the server never told clients the `ehcliAdoptable` marker was cleared, so the sessions grid kept the session in adoptable/read-only limbo and dropped the active cell.
- Server: `AgentHostStateManager.restoreSession` now emits a `sessionSummaryChanged` delta for a previously-surfaced session instead of silently overwriting the summary.
- Client: `baseAgentHostSessionsProvider._handleSessionSummaryChanged` applies a cleared `_meta` (via `hasOwnProperty`, like `activity`) and keeps `_metaByRawId` in sync so the passive session-state subscription reopens.

This is Agents-Window-only (the chat editor has no grid/active-session fallback or adoptable guard). Native/pure agent-host sessions are unaffected — the server delta only fires for surfaced-adoptable sessions.

### 4. Migration telemetry
Adds `agentHost.legacyCopilotCliMigration`, emitted **only when the migrate setting is ON**, with `outcome` = `migrated` | `skipped` | `failed` plus `success`, `turnCount`, `durationMs`, `hasProject`, `hasWorktree`, `workingDirectoryCount`, and `errorMessage` (failures). Enables metrics on attempted / succeeded / failed / didn't-migrate. `IAgent.ensureSessionAdopted` now returns `{ adopted, eligible }` so the host can distinguish a real migration candidate from an ordinary native restore.

### Tests
- `mapSessionEvents`: scaffolding-strip cases (wrapped / wrapper-only / empty-wrapper / plain).
- `worktreeIsolation`: `adoptExistingWorktreeMetadata` linked-worktree bridge + primary-checkout no-op.
- `agentHostStateManager`: surfaced→restore emits `sessionSummaryChanged` clearing the adoptable marker.
- `copilotAgent`: updated `ensureSessionAdopted` result-shape assertions.

### Notes
- No impact on the main chat scenario or other providers (Claude/Codex): the migration/telemetry/worktree paths are gated on the migrate flag / `adopted`, and `mapSessionEvents` is Copilot-only. The only always-on addition is `stripPromptScaffolding`, which runs on restore (not live streaming).

title: agentHost: widen native Claude setup detection
body:
`detectExistingClaudeSetup` recognized only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so several ordinary BYO-Anthropic setups read as "no local Claude" and got forced into a GitHub sign-in. This widens the `~/.claude/settings.json` validator — the single source of truth for the key set — with three more sources:

| Source | Why it counts |
| --- | --- |
| `env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` | First-class in Anthropic's own resolution order, immediately after `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. |
| `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Counts on its own: it points Claude at a gateway that supplies the credential. |
| `apiKeyHelper` (top-level) | A command the CLI runs to mint a key, so a setup can be complete with no credential stored anywhere. |

`apiKeyHelper` sits outside the `env` block, so `readClaudeSettingsEnv` became `readClaudeSettings` and returns the whole validated object. The env predicate and its derived type are renamed (`hasClaudeCredential` → `hasNativeClaudeEnv`, `ClaudeCredentialEnv` → `ClaudeNativeEnv`) since a base URL is an endpoint override rather than a credential.

Presence-only and empty-string-doesn't-count both still hold — nothing here reads a credential beyond asking whether it is a non-empty string. Confirmed `ObjValidator` iterates only declared properties, so a real settings file full of undeclared keys (`model`, `permissions`, `hooks`, …) still validates.

No self-detection loop with the proxy transport: it injects `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` into the SDK's *subprocess settings* env, not this process's, so its own plumbing can't read back as a native setup.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep 'claudeTransportMode'` — 4 passing (new coverage for all three sources on both the env-var and settings.json paths, plus empty-value, wrong-type, and undeclared-key cases).
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

Sniffing files and env vars is a hand-maintained reimplementation of the CLI's own credential resolution, and it's wrong in both directions:

- **False negative** — a user who runs `claude login` and never `claude setup-token` keeps their credential in the OS keychain, with no env var, no `settings.json` entry, and no `apiKeyHelper`. Detection says "no setup" while they are fully logged in.
- **False positive** — an inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing at loopback (another tool's local proxy) now reads as a gateway setup, which routes `native` and then fails inside the SDK.

The SDK exposes `Query.accountInfo()`, which returns the CLI's *own* resolution (`apiProvider: 'firstParty' | 'gateway' | 'bedrock' | …`) and drifts from it by construction never. It can't replace this outright — it needs a live `Query` (a spawned CLI subprocess), while `getProtectedResources()` and `_defaultTransportMode()` are both synchronous. The shape that works is two tiers: `accountInfo()` as the authority, called on the query `_fetchNativeModels` already opens (no extra spawn) and cached for the sync call sites, with this detection demoted to a cheap pre-filter that decides *whether to ask* — so a false positive costs one wasted spawn instead of a wrong sign-in gate.

title: [Perf] Fix retained snippet initialization work
body:
## Problem

`SnippetsService` starts asynchronous extension, user, and workspace snippet discovery after the workbench is restored. Workspace-folder and workbench-state changes enqueue additional workspace discovery promises in `_pendingWork`.

`_pendingWork` was an array that was cleared only when `getSnippets` or `getSnippetFiles` happened to join it. Agents Window session switches trigger workspace initialization, but they do not necessarily query snippets afterward. The initialization promises therefore settled successfully but remained strongly referenced by the array. In the memory campaign, 100 session switches left 106 settled promises under `SnippetsService._pendingWork` and correlated with approximately 0.92–1.00 MB of renderer growth per switch.

## Fix

Track initialization promises in a `Set` and remove each promise from the set as soon as it fulfills or rejects. This changes `_pendingWork` from a history of work that depends on a later consumer to drain it into a bounded collection of only currently in-flight work.

`_joinSnippets` snapshots the set without clearing it. As a result, concurrent snippet queries all wait for the same initialization work; the settlement handlers remain solely responsible for removal. Rejections are removed and logged while preserving the existing rejection seen by callers awaiting initialization.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/snippets/test/browser/snippetsService.test.ts` (32 passing, 1 pending)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/snippets/browser/snippetsService.ts`

1. Scroll down until the first prompt's own row passes above the top of the transcript. Verify the band appears only at that point, not while the prompt is still visible.
2. Verify the band names the prompt you scrolled past and that `N/M` matches its real position among your prompts.
3. Keep scrolling through several prompts. Verify the label swaps as each prompt passes the top, and that the label animates in the direction you are scrolling.
4. Scroll back to the very top. Verify the band goes away.
5. Click the label. Verify it jumps to that prompt and aligns it to the top of the transcript.
6. Use **Go to Previous Prompt** and **Go to Next Prompt** to step through prompts. Verify each target lands at the top and the label and count stay in sync.
7. Verify **Go to Previous Prompt** is disabled on the first prompt and **Go to Next Prompt** is disabled on the last.
8. Send a new prompt while the header is showing. Verify the count total grows and nothing is left stale.
9. Try a chat with exactly one prompt. Verify no header appears.
10. Try a very long prompt, a multi-line prompt, and a prompt containing only an attachment or whitespace. Verify the label stays on one line and truncates with an ellipsis rather than wrapping or stretching the band. A prompt with no text should read `(empty prompt)`.

## Setting

1. Set `"chat.stickyScroll.enabled": false`. Verify the header disappears without reloading the window.
2. Set it back to `true`. Verify it comes back and still tracks scrolling correctly.
3. Toggle it while several chats are open at once, including across both windows, and verify every open chat responds.

## Accessibility

1. With a screen reader, press `Alt+F1` in chat to open the accessibility help. Verify it describes the pinned prompt and the two navigation buttons.
2. Turn the setting off and reopen the help. Verify that description is gone. Also verify it is absent in Quick Chat, where no header is mounted.

title: Show output file for truncated shell output when instead of shell_exit preview for now
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329720
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596
Follow-up: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329724

The SDK built-in shell completion gives VS Code two representations of completed output:

- `tool.execution_complete.result.content` is display text produced by the runtime. When output spills to a file, this contains the "Output too large... Saved to: ..." message, the saved-file path, and instructions for inspecting it.
- The `shell_exit` content block is structured completion metadata. It carries `exitCode`, `outputTruncated`, and `outputPreview`; for spilled output, that preview is only a capped raw-output head and does not contain the saved-file path.

At completion the live non-PTY output channel is retired and the terminal card is rebuilt from the retained tool result. Previously the card always preferred `shell_exit.outputPreview`, so once `shell_exit` started reaching VS Code again, a large command finished by replacing the useful saved-file message with only the capped preview.

This PR uses the following selection policy:

- When `shell_exit.outputTruncated === true` and completion text exists, display `result.content` so the card shows where the full output was saved.
- Otherwise, prefer the structured `shell_exit.outputPreview`.
- If truncated completion text is unavailable, keep `outputPreview` as the fallback.
- Continue taking exit code and truncation state from structured `shell_exit` metadata; only the displayed text source changes.

This is an intentional bridge, not the final API shape. #329724 tracks adding a structured large-output artifact path or URI to the SDK/runtime contract. Once available, VS Code can render a dedicated user-facing link from typed data and stop depending on model-facing completion prose.

- Update terminal history/live-finalization mapping through the shared adapter policy.
- Keep legacy shell completion trailer stripping when completion text is selected.
- Cover truncated SDK shell completion with a regression test.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Retaining tool completion text alongside structured terminal content follows [`CopilotAgentSession` tool completion mapping](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e390f36f69fe6cdf1c1c3262f0b50f1d01552ec4/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L4090-L4126).
- The saved-file message comes from the runtime's [`format_shell_output`](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/blob/2147954ee33e4a98933cd617aa3aca383d261b20/src/runtime/src/tools/shell_tools.rs#L195-L211).
- Treating `outputPreview` as lossy when truncated follows the SDK wire contract, which states that it may be partial and is not guaranteed to contain full output: [`ExternalToolTextResultForLlmContentShellExit`](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/blob/2147954ee33e4a98933cd617aa3aca383d261b20/src/native/sdk-contract/src/api/rpc.rs#L5635-L5663).

When the Copilot runtime spills large shell output to a file, the tool completion text includes the saved-file path, while structured `shell_exit` content exposes only `outputPreview` and `outputTruncated`.

VS Code therefore has no typed way to surface or act on the full-output artifact. The immediate UI fix uses the tool completion display text when the structured preview is truncated, but deliberately does not parse a path out of that prose.

The public SDK/runtime contract should expose the large-output artifact location as structured shell completion data so consumers can render it without depending on presentation text.

title: agentHost: adding a Claude credential while gated at "Sign in to use Agents" needs a restart
body:
### Symptom

A signed-out user with no Anthropic credential opens the Agents window and hits the **"Sign in to use Agents"** gate. They then set up a Claude credential (an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in `~/.claude/settings.json` or the environment) and return to the window.

Nothing happens. The gate stays up until the app is restarted — even though the user now has exactly the setup the signed-out feature exists to serve.

### Why

The gate is `resolveAgentAuthRequirement`, which needs **both** halves to flip, and neither is reactive at agent level while no session exists:

1. **`protectedResources[].required`** — `ClaudeAgent.getProtectedResources()` reads the credential on demand, but agent infos are only republished on the `agents` observable, `onDidCustomizationsChange`, or `RootConfigChanged`. A credential file appearing triggers none of them.
2. **`models.length`** — `_refreshModels()` gates the native catalog on `detectExistingClaudeSetup`, so it would pick the credential up, but nothing calls it. `AgentModelRefreshScheduler._refreshActive` only ticks providers in `_activeSinceLastRefresh`, which is populated exclusively by `onDidStartTurn`. A gated user has never started a turn, so Claude is never refreshed. Catch-22.

`ClaudeCustomizationWatcher` does watch `<userHome>/.claude` recursively, but it's constructed per **session** (`claudeAgentSession.ts`) — and the gated scenario has zero sessions.

### Note on scope

Half of this is long-standing: before #329718 the same user was already stuck, via `models: 0` → `Unusable`. #329718 made `required` a second stale input but did not create the stuck state, and fixing only `required` would not unstick anyone, because the model count would still be `0`. **Both halves have to move together**, which is why it wasn't folded into that PR.

### Sketch

- Add an optional `onDidChangeProtectedResources?: Event<void>` to `IAgent`, wired in `AgentSideEffects._registerAgentListeners` next to `onDidCustomizationsChange` so it calls `_publishAgentInfos`. (Reusing `onDidCustomizationsChange` for this would work mechanically but is the wrong signal, and the repo guidance discourages events driving cross-component control flow.)
- Give `ClaudeAgent` an agent-lifetime watcher on the credential sources, firing that event **and** kicking `_startModelRefresh()` when usability actually flips, so both gate inputs update together.
- Prefer a correlated watcher (`fileService.createWatcher`) per the repo guideline, debounced like `ClaudeCustomizationWatcher`.

Worth checking whether Codex has the same shape for its own native providers.

Found during review of #329718 (thanks @copilot-pull-request-reviewer for spotting the reactivity gap).

body:
## Description

When the Agent Host process starts, it attempts to initialize its configuration from a `vscode-userdata:` URI even though the process file service only registers the disk-backed `file:` provider. The configuration watcher consequently fails before Agent Host providers finish initializing.

This prevents Agent Host from loading the default profile's user settings, including network settings such as `http.proxy` that its request stack depends on.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start VS Code Insiders with Agent Host enabled.
2. Start or restore an Agent Host session.
3. Inspect `agenthost.log` immediately after process startup.

## Actual Behavior

Startup logs contain errors similar to:

```text
Agent Host process started successfully
CodeExpectedError: ENOPRO: No file system provider found for resource 'vscode-userdata:<user-data>/User'
CodeExpectedError: ENOPRO: No file system provider found for resource 'vscode-userdata:<user-data>/User/settings.json'
```

The Agent Host `ConfigurationService` is created with `environmentService.userRoamingDataHome`, whose scheme is `vscode-userdata`. The Agent Host entry points register `Schemas.file`, but do not register a `vscode-userdata` provider, so the settings file cannot be watched or loaded.

## Expected Behavior

Agent Host should load the default profile's disk-backed `User/settings.json` without file-system-provider errors so settings required by Agent Host services are available at startup.

## Related

- Related to #329116, which contains the same startup error while reporting missing Claude models after the first Remote SSH connection.
- Related to #328736, where the same startup error was observed while investigating disappearing Remote SSH sessions.

title: agentHost: require GitHub for Claude unless a BYO-Anthropic setup exists
body:
Since #329331, `ClaudeAgent` advertised the GitHub Copilot protected resource as `required: false` **unconditionally**, reasoning that per-session routing means no host-global mode can make Copilot strictly required.

But `required` isn't a question about routing. It's read by exactly one thing — [`protectedResourcesRequireGitHubCopilotSignIn`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentService.ts#L976) — which backs the Agents window gate and the per-session-type gate. Answering "optional" for a user with **no Anthropic credential** claimed Claude was usable without GitHub, when every model the merged catalog can offer them is Copilot-routed.

This restores the pre-#329331 condition: **optional only when a local BYOK setup is discovered.**

## Change

New private `_hasUsableNativeSetup()` is the single "can Claude run without GitHub right now?" fact: the `allowSignedOutWhenUsable` opt-in **and** `detectExistingClaudeSetup` (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the process env or the `env` block of `~/.claude/settings.json`). `_defaultTransportMode()` now feeds `hasExistingSetup` from the same helper, so the advertised requirement and the fallback transport can't disagree.

Two deliberate choices worth review attention:

- **The resource is still _kept_ in the list rather than dropped.** `authenticateProtectedResources` matches on `resource` and ignores `required`, so the silent probe survives: an already-signed-in user still has a token forwarded (no prompt when signed out), and `authenticate()` still acquires the proxy handle that Copilot-routed models need.
- **Sign-in state is deliberately not an input.** Whether GitHub is *required* is a property of what the user can run without it, not of whether they happen to be connected at this instant. (The pre-#329331 expression also flipped back to required once a token arrived; this avoids that churn.)

Making this derived rather than constant introduces a staleness risk, since it now depends on live config + filesystem state. That's the main thing I went looking for — see run C below.

## Verification

Unit tests updated (the default-context assertion, plus two new tests covering the credential-present and opt-in-off branches). Full `platform/agentHost` suite passes (4339).

Verified end-to-end against a real **signed-out** Agents window (`--use-mock-keychain`), reading the published `protectedResources` off the AHP JSONL log:

| Run | Claude credential | opt-in | Published `required` | Window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | none | on | **`true`** | "Sign in to use Agents" gate |
| B | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | on | **`false`** | Opens signed out, Claude selected, 5 models, discovered-config nudge |
| C | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | off | **`true`** | Gate (kill switch holds) |

`codex` published `required=false` in all three runs — that's what `claude` was incorrectly mirroring before this fix.

Run C also exercised the staleness path. The host started with a stale `true` in its `agent-host-config.json`, so the initial publish was wrong — and then corrected itself:

```
23:12:48.771  initSnapshot   claude required=false      <- stale config at startup
23:12:48.778  configChanged: allowSignedOutWhenUsable=false
23:12:48.871  agentsChanged  claude required=true       <- republished 93ms later
23:12:50.245  agentsChanged  claude required=true models=5
```

So the derived value is safe: `AgentSideEffects` already republishes agent infos on `RootConfigChanged`, and `_publishAgentInfos`' `equals` guard limits the dispatch to real changes.

One note for reviewers: run B's models came from a **fake** API key. That isn't a flaw in the test — it confirms the existing comment in `_refreshModels` that the SDK's `supportedModels()` is a *static* catalog which answers without validating credentials. `required: false` + models > 0 is what lets the window open; a real turn would fail later. Pre-existing and untouched here.

title: Add Agent Host turn context telemetry
body:
## Overview

### What

Widens the existing per-turn Agent Host telemetry without changing its cadence:

- `agentHost.turnCompleted.isSubagentSession`
- `agentHost.turnFailed.isSubagentSession`
- `agentHost.turnCompleted.isBYOK`
- `agentHost.turnCompleted.interactionMode`

Interaction mode is captured from `SessionConfigKey.Mode` when a direct or queued turn starts and remains stable if session configuration changes while the turn is running. Subagent status is derived from the normalized owning session while the original chat URI continues to supply `chatSessionId`, preserving distinct nested chat identities. BYOK status is derived from the existing privacy-safe model telemetry kind; raw BYOK model identifiers remain represented as `byokModel`.

This does not change `copilotCli/response.*`, turn correlation, model-call counting, `ChatUsage` cadence, or `response.*.requestId` semantics.

### Why

This implements the Agent Host-owned portions of [microsoft/vscode#329684](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329684): main-versus-subagent analysis, privacy-safe BYOK analysis, and turn interaction mode. These dimensions naturally belong on the existing per-turn events and are already available in local turn context.

The detailed source and production-data audit was supplied as `telemetry-329684-audit.md` with the implementation handoff. It is not added to the repository because it contains internal aggregate validation notes.

## Property-by-property parity

| Field | Source or derivation | Parity |
|---|---|---|
| `turnCompleted.isSubagentSession` | Normalized Agent Host session plus the original subagent chat identity | ✅ Same main/subagent signal |
| `turnFailed.isSubagentSession` | Same derivation as the associated completion event | ✅ Same main/subagent signal |
| `turnCompleted.isBYOK` | `modelTelemetryKind`: `byok` → `true`; `trusted`/`unknown` → `false`; unavailable → omitted | ✅ Same BYOK signal without model-ID disclosure |
| `turnCompleted.interactionMode` | `SessionConfigKey.Mode` snapshotted at turn start | ✅ Same bounded `interactive`/`plan`/`autopilot` signal |

## Measurement-by-measurement parity

No duration, token, or call-count measurements are added or changed. The new boolean dimensions use the repository's existing GDPR `isMeasurement` convention for telemetry booleans.

## Row-count and dashboard implications

- Population remains the existing Agent Host turn population across providers.
- Cadence remains one `turnCompleted` row per tracked turn and one `turnFailed` diagnostic row for failures.
- No new telemetry events or duplicate rows are introduced.
- Existing `provider + agentSessionId + chatSessionId + turnId` correlation remains unchanged.
- `isBYOK` is absent when no model context exists rather than using a placeholder.
- Existing timing, resolved-Auto model reporting, permission level, and error fields retain their semantics.

## Semantic-shift ledger

There are no close-analogue mappings in this change; all four fields are derived from the existing Agent Host turn/session state at the same lifecycle boundary.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostTurnTelemetry.test.ts` (21 passing)
## CI follow-up

The macOS Electron integration job exposed tracked Codex issue [#329512](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329512): the workspace-list shell command succeeds and the final response contains both filenames, but the completed AHP tool call intermittently has empty result text. The strict test is now gated only for deterministic Codex replay on macOS; recording, Windows, and other-provider coverage remain enabled, while Linux was already gated for Codex shell replay.

Fixes #330386

Fixes Agent Host per-turn change summaries attributing repository changes made between turns to the next agent response.

A real long-lived session reproduced this after the checkout advanced between turns: the UI reported 1030 files / +45890 -10554 for a turn that differed from `main` by one CSS file.

- Capture the working tree immediately before sending each turn to the agent.
- Create a missing first-turn baseline synchronously from that pre-turn tree.
- Parent the end-of-turn checkpoint to the matching turn-start snapshot, so Git-backed summaries represent start-to-end changes only.
- Avoid whole-tree Git attribution while peer turns overlap, since shared-working-tree edits cannot be separated; fall back to the exact owning chat's tracked file edits instead.
- Reject duplicate turn IDs across chats in one session, resolving restored peer histories before validation so checkpoint ownership remains unambiguous.
- Serialize checkpoint cleanup with capture and cover client/provider cancellation, terminal errors, error-followed-by-completion, truncation, session deletion, and peer-chat disposal.
- Preserve authoritative empty/no-op changesets and legacy reused checkpoint refs.

## Validation

- Focused Agent Host suites: 406 passing, 55 pending.
- ESLint, client type-check, and layer validation pass.
- Manual Code OSS end-to-end runs in both the Editor and Agents windows verified that an external commit between turns is excluded from the second response summary.

title: Agent Host Copilot startup repeatedly fails when native runtime cannot load

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
## Summary

The new Agent Host Copilot provider can repeatedly fail before serving any user turn because the Copilot CLI's native runtime cannot load. The largest actionable failure family is concentrated on old Windows builds:

- Windows build 10240: Windows 10 1507/RTM, released July 29, 2015 (about 11 years old as of August 2026).
- Windows build 14393: Windows 10 1607 / Windows Server 2016, released August 2, 2016 (about 10 years old as of August 2026).

The build number alone does not identify the edition. Consumer Windows 10 releases on these builds are long out of support, while Enterprise LTSB and Server editions have different support timelines.

## Impact observed

I investigated aggregate `monacoworkbench/agenthost.copilotclientfailure` telemetry for `failureKind=startupFailed`, `operation=startClient`.

Frozen reproducible snapshot:

- Server-upload window: 2026-08-06 00:00 through 2026-08-07 13:00 UTC.
- Ingestion cutoff: 2026-08-07 19:15 UTC.
- 667 rows, 662 distinct startup attempts, 55 affected machines, and 94 sessions.
- Five rows were exact duplicate ingestion records.
- Per-machine attempts: median 2, P90 37, P95 71, maximum 118.
- Four machines had at least 50 startup failures.
- Median same-session retry gap was 27 seconds.
- Almost every physical attempt had a distinct `clientFailureId`, so the high counts are repeated startups rather than duplicate telemetry.
- No affected machine later emitted Agent Host user-message, turn-completed, or Copilot response-success telemetry during the examined window.

The strongest environment concentrations were:

- Linux kernel 5.14.0: 20 of 26 active Insider machines were affected.
- Windows builds 10240 and 14393 were disproportionately affected.

Failures occurred with both Copilot CLI 1.0.78 and 1.0.79-2, so 1.0.79-2 is not the sole introduction.

## Native Windows failure family

The apparent missing-module message is misleading:

- 294 events on 14 machines mentioned the loader's root fallback name, `runtime.win32-x64-msvc.node`.
- 18 events on one machine mentioned the packaged path, `prebuilds/win32-x64/runtime.node`.
- The inspected 1.0.78, 1.0.79-2, and 1.0.79-6 packages correctly contain `prebuilds/win32-x64/runtime.node`.
- VS Code's Copilot packaging rules retain the selected platform package and its native prebuilds.
- The native addon loader first tries `prebuilds/win32-x64/runtime.node`. When that load fails, it tries the nonexistent root-level fallback. The final `Cannot find module` text therefore obscures the real first load error.

Within this family, aggregate message analysis found:

- 220 events where the packaged native runtime failed with "The specified procedure could not be found."
- 60 events where the runtime failed with a DLL initialization error.
- Remaining cases had other native-load errors.

The procedure failures were concentrated on the old Windows builds. PE import inspection of the packaged runtime found direct sandbox/AppContainer API imports, including `DeriveCapabilitySidsFromName`. This makes an unavailable imported Windows API or eagerly linked sandbox dependency a strong root-cause candidate. The exact missing procedure has not yet been conclusively proven.

CLI 1.0.79-6 changed native exception-filter cleanup, but no observed build in the frozen telemetry window launched that version.

## Other failure families

The same startup telemetry population also contains:

- Linux/macOS permission failures.
- Windows native child-process crashes.
- Native DLL initialization failures distinct from the old-build procedure failures.

These may require separate fixes once bounded telemetry provides stable breakdowns.

## Retry behavior

`CopilotAgent._ensureClient` clears its shared startup promise after rejection and has no cooldown, backoff, or circuit breaker. Independent session/model refresh triggers can therefore repeatedly launch the same client in a persistently broken environment.

Current telemetry reflects each attempt but does not connect repeated attempts into one outage:

- `clientFailureId` identifies one physical startup attempt.
- There is no outage-level ID or attempt ordinal.
- `activeTurnCount=0` and `recoveryStarted=false` are expected for startup failures.
- Existing recovery telemetry covers closed-connection teardown/replacement flow, not successful recovery from startup failure.

## Suggested fixes

### Copilot CLI/native runtime

1. Confirm the oldest supported Windows client/server builds for the native runtime.
2. Reproduce native loading on builds 10240 and 14393, including supported LTSB/Server editions where applicable.
3. Identify the exact unavailable import or initialization dependency.
4. Either:
   - remove/delay-load the unsupported sandbox dependency,
   - provide a compatible fallback,
   - or fail once with a clear unsupported-platform error.
5. Preserve the first native-addon load error instead of allowing the missing fallback module to become the dominant message.

### VS Code Agent Host

1. Add bounded startup-failure cause, resource, and process-exit-code fields so aggregate analysis does not depend on raw exception text.
2. Include SDK startup timeouts and classify `EACCES`/`EPERM` as permission failures.
3. Add bounded retry/backoff or a startup circuit breaker for persistent failures.
4. Consider an outage ID, attempt ordinal, exhaustion event, and successful-start/recovery event.

A draft PR will add the bounded telemetry from items 1 and 2. Product retry behavior should be handled separately because it changes runtime behavior and needs focused tests.

(Written by Copilot)

title: agentHost: keep the native Claude catalog published through first sign-in
body:
Follow-up to #328990, which added `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable`. The setting did not reliably suppress the sign-in dialog.

### The bug

`ClaudeAgent._onAuthToken` blanked the model catalog unconditionally before kicking off the refresh for the new token:

```ts
oldHandle?.dispose();
this._models.set([], undefined);
void this._startModelRefresh();
```

On a **replacement** token that is correct — a different account can have different model entitlements, so the stale list must not survive a failed enumeration.

On a **first** sign-in it is not. There is no superseded account to drop, and the catalog being cleared is the account-independent native bootstrap list. Blanking there publishes an empty catalog for the length of the refresh.

The Agents window reads an agent with no models as `SessionTypeAuthRequirement.Unusable`, so that empty window closes the `allowSignedOutWhenUsable` gate mid-startup and forces the sign-in dialog on a user who is already signing in — the GitHub session resolves before the Copilot default account does, so the welcome flow still believes it is signed out.

### The fix

Blank only when replacing an existing handle.

### Verification

Unit: new test holds CAPI enumeration open with a `DeferredPromise` and asserts the catalog stays published across the pending window. Negative control confirmed — reverting the fix yields `whileEnumerating: []`. Full `ClaudeAgent` suite: 241 passing.
